analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only. They touch docs/operations/provider-release.md (head lines 482-922, including the new Cluster Runtime Facts section at 649-795) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (Qwen27 TP assistant paragraph near line 2456, plus a date bump). Neither file changes executable code, a workflow or a policy, so I found no concrete security regression.

What the docs describe, and the controls I checked in the text:
- The cluster_runtime block is gated by per-environment *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED variables (lines 718-727) and is sent only when the coordinator accepts it (749-753).
- The facts step removes secret-derived env values and deletes the signing keychain before any release code runs (673-677).
- The final CLI runs with env -i (680).
- Only the public catalog and CDN are fetched, never weights (687-695).
- validate caps the body at 64 KiB and the derived ID lengths (731-740).
- The text states that official registration does not authorize a provider to serve (619-620). This is consistent with the TB-011 and T-052/T-054 posture.
- The dev-branch lane section (488-558) says that the dev branch has no pull_request rule today (527-531) and that secrets: inherit is used. It also says a dev push gets the Developer ID signature. This is a documented, pre-existing-style gap that the text itself flags for an administrator. The workflow files are not in this batch, so the claim that the guard pins non-dev secrets (516-520) is unverified here.

Unverified contracts for later passes:
- The actual workflow YAML, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, and the platform's cluster-approval derivation from releases (EIGENINFERENCE_CLUSTER_PAIR_APPROVALS_FROM_RELEASES) are not supplied.
- A release-derived approval and grant mechanism (631-665) is a new trust path from pipeline-authenticated release registration to public cluster routing. It should be reviewed on the platform side against T-053, T-054 and T-055.
- The cli-reference change states that the Qwen27 assistant is unqualified for public traffic and is excluded under auto. That is conservative and consistent with T-056's overclaim concerns.

Overall, no threat-model contradictions are visible in these docs.
